content:
Google is about to impose restrictions on which Gemini models free users and AI Plus subscribers can access, following a revised compute usage policy introduced in May.

According to support documents updated this week, Gemini App users without a Google AI subscription will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. From 9 October, non-paying users will lose access to (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

AI Plus subscribers, meanwhile, will be limited to Flash-Lite and Flash, with the Pro model no longer available. These users, who pay US$4.99 per month, will "receive an email explaining when the change takes effect."

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

AI Pro and AI Ultra users are unaffected. In fact, customers on the US$19.99 monthly plan will gain access to the Deep Think option, offering "maximum parallel reasoning," a feature currently reserved for the US$99.99 and US$199.99 monthly tiers.

Top liked comment from Glitter Guru:

Argon had better replace Pro, otherwise I expect 4 Pro to launch alongside Argon when it goes public. If not, with ancient 3.1 Pro being the top model for most users, I'll be cancelling the Pro plan.

Gemini 3.1 Pro with Deep Think on AI Ultra

In October, the Gemini App also appears set to add "Low," "Medium" and "High" reasoning intensity options, "available for every model that can be used."

At present, users can only toggle on an "Extended Thinking: Complex Problem Solving" feature. The three new reasoning intensity tiers will mirror those already offered in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

How Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned remains unclear. Google announced earlier this week that Argon will be available first to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or sit in an entirely new tier above Pro.
